source.title: From Forest to Farm: Modeling Nitrogen Dynamics for Sustainable Agriculture
source.mode: informed redesign; source overview seen, not blind

execution.deliverable: original raster overview + exact production prompt + source evidence + review

claim: A conserved forest nitrogen-cycle model is progressively extended with seasonal farm management and a multispecies food web, enabling management-scenario comparison before formulating sustainable-agriculture recommendations.

paper_figure_signature.topology: FENCM -> AENCM -> AE-FW-NCM -> parallel management scenarios -> evaluation and sensitivity -> guidance; literature-supported extensions separately scoped
paper_figure_signature.novelty: Common nitrogen bookkeeping ties ecosystem succession, species interactions and farm management together
paper_figure_signature.input: compartments and modeled species interactions; representative parameter choices
boundaries: Forest total N is assumed conserved; agricultural N has external inputs/outputs
Bat pollination is a scenario extension
Nitrogen turnover is the paper's proxy, not externally validated stability
Rhizobia/legumes and straw reuse are literature-supported recommendations

narrative_map.first_glance: Natural nitrogen cycling becomes a managed multispecies farm model.
narrative_map.working: Track what each extension adds and how alternative management scenarios are evaluated.
narrative_map.technical: Equations/parameters remain in Sections 4-8; no generated empirical plots.
narrative_map.reading_logic: left-to-right model inheritance, then downstream analysis band

abstraction_map.invariant: producer/consumer losses return to organic N, decomposition returns inorganic N

abstraction_map.visual: crops/weeds, seasonal influence, sowing, harvest, fertilizer, chemical-use condition
abstraction_map.invariant: open N budget; intervention and competition are not trophic transfer
all nine prey-to-predator edges; C connects only crops/weeds; shared environment retained

abstraction_map.visual: alternative scenarios -> two N metrics and sensitivity

predation A, assimilation B transpose, competition C transpose, producer uptake Ninorg*R and mortality Gamma acting on N

equation_operand_ledger.role: N transformation integral and H/I; paper calls turnover a stability indicator
equation_operand_ledger.encoding: named metrics only; no invented values or generic external-validation claim

equation_operand_ledger.role: bat population contributes to crop growth

equation_operand_ledger.encoding: straw reuse recommendation, not a simulated feedback

evidence_ledger.reuse: No empirical pixels sent for generative redraw; original symbolic scenes only
evidence_ledger.budget: 0% numeric evidence; scoped overview of modeling/analysis rather than result figure
evidence_ledger.limitations: No model rerun; no generalization of paper's ecological claims beyond its assumptions
